OPS_033.context: Two brands of waterproofing with almost identical packaging were noticed in the warehouse.
OPS_033.text: How will you prevent the wrong item being issued?

options.A: I will compare the item codes, certificates and areas of use in the specification.
options.B: I will tell the warehouse that issue must be suspended until the batches are separated.
options.C: I will check the labelling and arrange separate storage with clear labels.
options.D: I will put the batches in separate places and send a request to the engineer.

OPS_034.context: The transport company offers to deliver ventilation units at night with no receiving staff present.

options.A: I will arrange a new delivery time slot and coordinate everyone's attendance.
options.B: I will check the unloading requirements and schedule receipt within an authorised time slot.
options.C: I will ask for the truck's arrival to be moved to a daytime slot when the ramp is available.
options.D: I will agree a realistic unloading time with security, the warehouse and the transport company.

OPS_035.context: After the rain, some boxes of electrical equipment got wet under the tarpaulin.
OPS_035.text: How will you organise assessment of the batch?

options.A: I will involve the electricians and the warehouse in a joint inspection and decision.
options.B: I will mark the damaged spots and put the batch in a dry area until it is inspected.
options.C: I will check the packaging and documents against the storage conditions for each item.
options.D: I will assess the damage with a specialist and set aside the disputed boxes.

OPS_036.context: The supplier is pushing for urgent confirmation of the order, although price approval is not yet complete.

options.A: I will ask them to reserve the goods until approval is complete.
options.B: I will give the decision date and speed up the documentary approval without skipping steps.
options.C: I will check the limit and go through the purchase approval route.
options.D: I will explain directly that the order will be confirmed after the terms are approved.

OPS_037.context: Air ducts arrived on site with a data sheet specifying a different sheet metal thickness.
OPS_037.text: How will you check whether the delivery is fit for use?

options.A: I will compare the actual marking, the data sheet and the design specification.
options.B: I will set aside the disputed batch and file a claim according to the procedure.
options.C: I will check the thickness and documents, then formalise acceptance or rejection.
options.D: I will leave the batch in the quarantine area and call the HVAC (OViK) engineer.

OPS_038.context: A driver reports that the unloading area is occupied by machinery, and his truck is blocking the entrance.
OPS_038.text: How will you resolve the situation?

options.A: I will assign a safe parking spot and clarify a new unloading time with the participants.
options.B: I will take on coordinating the entry and designate a safe waiting area.
options.C: I will ask the driver to wait in the approved area and warn the dispatcher.
options.D: I will connect the driver, the machinery dispatcher and the warehouse to clear the area.

OPS_039.context: Two sites are demanding the last pumps from the warehouse at the same time.
OPS_039.text: How will you set the priority?

options.A: I will openly present the shortage to the managers and propose a justified order.
options.B: I will reserve the pumps until an authorised person agrees the allocation.
options.C: I will compare the approved schedules, installation dates and availability of alternative batches.
options.D: I will prepare a comparison of deadlines and agree the decision with the site managers.

OPS_040.context: Thermal insulation arrived without some of the accompanying documents, and installation is in a week.
OPS_040.text: How will you organise further actions?

options.A: I will place the batch separately and remind the supplier of the list of documents.
options.B: I will request the missing documents and agree a backup installation date with the team.
options.C: I will agree a date for the complete document package with the supplier, the warehouse and the supervisor.
options.D: I will not issue the batch until confirmed documents arrive.

OPS_041.context: Deliveries to the cast-in-place section often end with leftovers that are not reflected in the orders.
OPS_041.text: How will you improve the purchasing plan?

options.A: I will compare consumption rates, actual yield and leftovers over several cycles.
options.B: I will discuss with the site manager the reasons for the leftovers and updating the weekly requirement.
options.C: I will check the consumption history together with the section and adjust the order.
options.D: I will propose a weekly reconciliation of leftovers with the supervisor.

OPS_042.context: The specification names a specific brand of fixing, while the contractor offers an equivalent it has in stock.

options.A: I will set out the necessary documents and send the equivalent for approval.
options.B: I will explain that substitution is possible only after technical approval.
options.C: I will keep the original order and pass the proposal to the project engineer.
options.D: I will check the set of documents and the approval route for the equivalent.

OPS_043.context: When issuing a batch of pipes, different heat numbers were found inside one package.

options.A: I will separate the batches in the records and arrange separate issue.
options.B: I will put the package on hold for a check and inform the plumbing (VK) engineer.
options.C: I will check the marking of each group against the certificates and design requirements.
options.D: I will check the certificates and separate the pipes by number before issue.

OPS_044.context: The supplier missed the agreed concrete delivery window, and the crew has already prepared the formwork.
OPS_044.text: How will you coordinate with the participants?

options.A: Once I get a new time from the plant, I will pass it to the site manager and the laboratory.
options.B: I will openly report the delay and clarify a feasible schedule together with the team.
options.C: I will connect the plant, the laboratory, the site manager and the dispatcher to agree a plan.
options.D: I will report the real delivery time and the restrictions of the new window myself.

OPS_045.context: The forwarder proposed a shorter route for long beams through a residential street.
OPS_045.text: How will you assess the route?

options.A: I will check the size restrictions, permits and turning conditions.
options.B: I will point out that dispatch is possible only along a permitted route.
options.C: I will check the route documents and justify the approved option to the driver.
options.D: I will keep the planned route and request a check from the transport department.

OPS_046.context: The forklift is needed at the same time by the warehouse and the finishers to move pallets.
OPS_046.text: How will you agree its use?

options.A: I will record the order of use and jointly choose suitable time slots.
options.B: I will check the usage plan and set up time slots.
options.C: I will pass the requests to the dispatcher and notify the teams of the decision.
options.D: I will collect the requests of both teams and agree a sequence without downtime.

OPS_047.context: In the monthly report, insulation write-offs increased while the volume of work stayed the same.
OPS_047.text: How will you deal with the deviation?

options.A: I will discuss likely sources of the discrepancy with the storekeeper and the supervisor.
options.B: I will pass the report to the warehouse and production for a joint reconciliation.
options.C: I will compare receipts, issues, returns and the actual area insulated.
options.D: I will check the accounting operations together with the section and clarify the real requirement.

OPS_048.context: An emergency delivery requires a payment not covered by the purchasing limit.
OPS_048.text: How will you formalise the decision?

options.A: I will request standard delivery and pass the proposal to speed it up to the manager.
options.B: I will explain the delivery options and formalise approval of the chosen rate.
options.C: I will prepare a calculation and go through the approval route for the extra payment.
options.D: I will tell the initiator that the expense requires separate approval.

OPS_049.context: In the network schedule, facade work starts before the fixing tests are complete.
OPS_049.text: How will you fix the dependency?

options.A: I will check the construction sequence and the conditions for authorising work specified in the design.
options.B: I will update the task links and issue a new version of the schedule.
options.C: I will check the test conditions and enter the confirmed dependency into the schedule.
options.D: I will flag the conflict and send it to the project manager for a decision.

OPS_050.context: The contractor promises to make up a week's delay but has not presented a plan.
OPS_050.text: How will you discuss the contractor's promise?

options.A: I will clearly request a calculation and jointly confirm verifiable milestones.
options.B: I will ask for specific shifts, volumes and resources and set a deadline for the answer.
options.C: I will schedule a meeting and ask the contractor to send a weekly plan.
options.D: I will gather the supervisors and the contractor to agree a realistic plan together.

OPS_051.context: The report shows 90% completion of the building services, but the test certificates have not yet been signed.
OPS_051.text: How will you assess the real progress?

options.A: I will tell the client that the completion percentage needs to be clarified.
options.B: I will request a list of unconfirmed stages from the engineers.
options.C: I will separate installation, testing and acceptance based on confirmed volumes.
options.D: I will check the confirmations and openly present the adjusted status.

OPS_052.context: A layout change affects three contracting organisations and the overall handover date for the floor.
OPS_052.text: How will you start revising the schedule?

options.A: I will send the change to the participants and ask them to update their schedules.
options.B: I will record the change, collect the adjacent trades' timings and propose a new plan.
options.C: I will hold a meeting of the adjacent trades and clarify the available work windows.
options.D: I will formalise the change and update the baseline schedule after agreement on its impact.

OPS_053.context: In weekly reports, adjacent trades calculate room readiness differently.
OPS_053.text: How will you work out a single rule?

options.A: I will check the readiness criteria against the contract milestones and the acceptance scope.
options.B: I will discuss with the teams clear signs that each room is complete.
options.C: I will propose common criteria after reviewing the disputed rooms with the contractors.
options.D: I will collect the current definitions and schedule a working meeting.

OPS_054.context: At a meeting, the manager proposes accepting an unrealistic date without assessing resources.

options.A: I will voice the risk and prepare a confirmed calculation for the decision.
options.B: I will firmly point out the resource risk and propose a date after the calculation.
options.C: I will record the date as preliminary and agree a check of resources.
options.D: I will check the volumes and available crews before updating the schedule.

OPS_055.context: The slab pour is planned for the day the independent inspection service will inspect the formwork.
OPS_055.text: How will you reflect the dependency in the plan?

options.A: I will put the pour after the confirmed inspection in the working schedule.
options.B: I will mark the pour as conditional and notify the batching plant.
options.C: I will clarify the inspection time, the conditions for authorising work and possible reasons for postponement.
options.D: I will check the duration of the inspection and schedule the transition only after approval.

OPS_056.context: An adjacent trade asks for two days of access to a shaft already occupied by another crew.
OPS_056.text: How will you resolve the conflict between time slots?

options.A: I will ask each crew for its minimum scope and propose a meeting.
options.B: I will openly point out the conflict and allocate access by stages with the teams.
options.C: I will bring both crews and the shaft supervisor together to allocate the time jointly.
options.D: I will set out the priority rules and the deadline by which an agreed plan is needed.

OPS_057.context: The contractor reported that the lift delivery has been postponed, but the delay is not reflected in the monthly forecast.
OPS_057.text: How will you recalculate the forecast?

options.A: I will check the critical path, the float and the related commissioning work.
options.B: I will inform management of the likely impact on the commissioning date.
options.C: I will recalculate the dependencies and present management with a new forecast and its assumptions.
options.D: I will note the risk in the register and request a confirmed delivery date.

OPS_058.context: After an internal partition was moved, some already closed work orders need to be reviewed.
OPS_058.text: How will you organise change control?

options.A: I will formalise the change and clarify the remaining volumes together with the contractors.
options.B: I will record the review of volumes, milestones and approvals in the change log.
options.C: I will request updated volumes from the technical department (PTO) and put the task in the plan.
options.D: I will gather the technical department (PTO) and the contractor to reconcile what has actually been done.

OPS_059.context: In finishing works, handover of concealed work before structures are closed up is regularly skipped.
OPS_059.text: How will you build the check into the schedule?

options.A: I will agree the inspection time and the form of the readiness signal with the supervisors.
options.B: I will remind the contractors to submit inspection requests in advance.
options.C: I will find the areas where the control point is missing from the sequence.
options.D: I will add inspection points and discuss their realistic duration with the teams.

OPS_060.context: The client asks for a daily status of the site, although data is collected once a week.

options.A: I will propose a daily status on critical milestones with the data source.
options.B: I will agree a short set of verifiable indicators and regular submission.
options.C: I will assign responsible people and a daily update deadline according to the procedure.
options.D: I will clarify which indicators can be reliably confirmed every day.

OPS_061.context: According to the schedule, window installation will start before the openings have been measured.
OPS_061.text: How will you clarify the start of work?

options.A: I will check the scope of the measurements and the deadlines for adjusting the products.
options.B: I will link the start of installation to the measurement report and update the plan.
options.C: I will recalculate the start based on confirmed measurements and formalise the schedule change.
options.D: I will note the dependency and ask the contractor for the measurement date.

OPS_062.context: The section manager reports that the same installers are included in the plans of two buildings.
OPS_062.text: How will you settle the resource conflict?

options.A: I will present the conflict at a meeting and reallocate shifts together with the site managers.
options.B: I will point out that double assignment is impossible and propose prioritising by milestones.
options.C: I will ask each site manager to confirm how many crew members are needed and when.
options.D: I will gather the site managers to agree shifts and sequence.

OPS_063.context: The actual masonry rate has been below plan for three weeks in a row, and the reports attribute this to the weather.
OPS_063.text: How will you check the cause of the deviation?

options.A: I will tell the managers that the cause needs to be checked before speeding up.
options.B: I will review the deviation with the site manager and the contractor.
options.C: I will compare the weather, work area availability, crew size and daily output.
options.D: I will collect the indicators and present a justified cause with options for measures.

OPS_064.context: To issue working documentation, the designer needs data from several contractors.
OPS_064.text: How will you organise data collection?

options.A: I will send out a single list of data and remind them of the response deadlines.
options.B: I will set up a register and organise a short meeting on dependencies.
options.C: I will help the contractors agree the format and procedure for passing on information.
options.D: I will create a request register with responsible people and deadlines.
